Name: Carly Lynch
Notes:
Hi, good afternoon! My name is Carly and I work with Bridging Voice, a nonprofit dedicated to providing communication and quality-of-life support for people with ALS, a neurodegenerative disease that results in paralysis and loss of ability to speak. We're hosting an innovation showcase (cocktail-style event) on May 28 at a restaurant in the East Village to introduce donors and community members to the technology we create and customize for ALS patients (https://bridgingvoice.org/launch-nys/). 

While this is a fundraising event, we’re looking to stay away from a traditional gala feel. We will have 4 different interactive stations set up throughout the restaurant space, where guests can engage with the technology and custom tools that we develop for our clients with ALS and learn more about our work. We’re aiming for fun and inspiring, as many of the guests will be new to our organization and possibly unfamiliar with ALS.

There will also be a brief, 30-min remarks portion of the night, where we will be honoring our board chair and founder, Peter Bloom, who has made extraordinary contributions to our organization — work that has genuinely changed the lives of thousands of people living with ALS. Peter is extremely humble and isn't exactly thrilled about being in the spotlight, so we want to make the award presentation something unexpected and memorable rather than a traditional podium moment. He is a bit of a magician as a hobby, and we actually have a magician joining to help present the award to him. We think it will make for a special and unique moment! 

We have a photographer for the event, but our board has just decided that they would like us to have videography as well, so that we can capture the remarks and award presentation, as well as the guests’ engagement at the different innovation stations. I know it’s last minute, but wondering if you might be available? Here are the event details:
Date: Thursday, May 28
Time: 6:30-9:30pm
Location: Next Door by Wegmans (770 Broadway, New York, NY 10003)
Expected attendance: 75-110 guests

We would be looking for a short (3-5min max) video recap of the night, with some highlights from the remarks and some footage of the stations that captures the impact of our work. The video will only be shared with attendees, but we’d love to be able to use some of the footage of the stations on our website and social media platforms separately if possible. 

If this sounds like a fit and you’re available on the 28th, I’d love to connect and get a quote. Thanks so much, and looking forward to hearing from you!

Wide and medium shots that show her in the event environment, including the stage, panel table, podium, signage, branding, audience, and room context where appropriate.

1. Lightly stylized brand images
A few more editorial-style images if the setting allows, such as her standing confidently in the venue, walking through the space, reviewing notes, looking composed before speaking, or positioned near visually interesting New Orleans/event backdrops.

Overall feel: professional, warm, confident, polished, authentic, and executive. We want the photos to look high-quality and brand-building without feeling overly staged or stiff.

Please prioritize clean composition, flattering angles, strong lighting, natural expressions, and images that communicate leadership, credibility, approachability, and presence.

We are looking for polished video coverage of my wife’s keynote/speaking engagement that can be used for a future speaker reel, press kit, professional bio materials, LinkedIn content, internal work visibility, and broader executive brand positioning.

The primary goal is to capture her as a confident, credible, warm, and engaging executive speaker. We want footage that documents the full keynote while also creating strong visual assets that can later be edited into a high-quality sizzle reel.

Please capture the following:

1. Full keynote address
Please record the full keynote from beginning to end with clean, stable framing and high-quality audio. This is the top priority. Ideally, we would like one reliable main angle and, if possible, additional cutaway angles for editing variety.

Please prioritize clear audio, clean lighting, steady framing, and enough coverage to allow the full address to be preserved and also edited into shorter clips.

1. Strong speaker moments
Please capture close, medium, and wide shots of her speaking, making key points, smiling, reacting, pausing, engaging the audience, and commanding the room. We want moments that visually communicate leadership, confidence, warmth, credibility, and presence.

1. Stage/platform coverage
Please capture footage of her on stage, at the podium, seated on a dais or panel if applicable, walking to the platform, being introduced, acknowledging the audience, and exiting the stage. Please also capture room context, event signage, sponsor/organization branding, audience size, applause, and any environmental details that help establish the significance of the event.

1. Staged or lightly directed B-roll
If time allows, please capture a few polished, lightly staged shots that can be used in a speaker reel, such as:
- Walking confidently toward the stage or through the venue
- Reviewing notes before speaking
- Standing in a strong executive posture near the stage or event signage
- Greeting attendees
- Waving or acknowledging the room
- Walking off stage after the talk
- A composed “pre-keynote” moment
- A confident “post-keynote” moment

These should feel natural, polished, and cinematic, not overly scripted.

1. Behind-the-scenes footage
Please capture BTS moments before and after the keynote, including her preparing, interacting with event organizers, speaking with attendees, greeting people, laughing, shaking hands, answering questions, taking photos, and engaging in natural conversations.

1. Audience and reaction shots
Please capture audience reactions, applause, people listening attentively, nodding, laughing, taking notes, and engaging with her remarks. These reaction shots will be important for editing the final sizzle reel and showing that her message resonated.

1. Short-form content opportunities
Please keep an eye out for moments that would work well as short clips for LinkedIn, Instagram, internal company communications, or promotional use. If there are strong soundbites, audience reactions, or powerful visual moments, please make sure those are captured cleanly.

Overall feel: professional, warm, executive, polished, cinematic, credible, and inspiring. The footage should position her as a strong leader, compelling speaker, and high-level professional presence.

The final use case is a speaker/sizzle reel, press kit, speaker kit, social media content, and future professional branding materials, so please capture with editing flexibility in mind.

Notes:
Photography and Videography Brief
SuperSkills Book Launch — Thursday 2 July 2026

Event overview
I'm launching my book SuperSkills: The Seven Human Skills for the Age of AI (Kogan Page) at the Ismaili Centre, South Kensington, on the evening of Thursday 2 July 2026. The book publishes the following morning. The launch is the central event of the campaign and the imagery from the night will be used in press coverage, my permanent author archive, social channels, future speaker reels, and ongoing book marketing for at least two years.
The brief below covers what I need photographically and what I'd like to discuss for video. I'm asking for a single quote that covers both, and a separate quote for photography only, so I can compare options.

The event in one paragraph
Approximately 200 guests in the Social Hall at the Ismaili Centre. The evening combines a hosted fireside conversation, two short readings, drinks and mingling, and a book signing. The room will include senior figures from publishing, business, media, and public life, alongside friends, family, and community guests. The tone of the evening is warm, considered, and culturally significant rather than corporate.

Logistics

Photographers should be briefed on respectful conduct in such a space. Photography permissions will be confirmed with the venue events lead in advance.

Programme (running order)
TimeMomentCoverage priority6:30 pmPre-event reception in side room (endorsers, press, senior guests)High — these are the guests of honour7:00 pmDoors open, drinks and mingling, optional Centre toursMedium7:50 pmGuests take seatsLow8:00 pmMC welcome by my eldest daughter (~5 minutes)High8:05 pmReading from the prologue by my younger daughter (~3 minutes)Highest — this is the emotional centre of the evening8:08 pmFireside conversation (35 minutes) hosted by Chin-RuHigh8:43 pmQ&A (10 minutes)Medium8:53 pmMC close and thanksLow8:55 pmSigning and continued minglingHigh9:30 pmWind downLow

Photography brief
Required shots — these must be captured
Pre-event and setup

One clean portrait of me in the Social Hall before guests arrive (5–10 minutes, around 6:30 pm)
One portrait of me holding the book against the architecture of the Centre
One wide shot of the Social Hall set up and empty, with the fireside chairs and lectern in position

Pre-event reception (6:30–7:00 pm)

Candid coverage of conversations in the side room
Group shot of endorsers and senior guests if a natural moment arises (not posed unless requested)

Arrival and mingling (7:00–7:50 pm)

Wide shots of guests arriving and the room filling
Detail shots — drinks, the book on display, the dhow on the fireside table, the architecture
Candid conversation shots, particularly of named guests (a guest list with marked priority names will be provided in advance)

Programme (8:00–8:53 pm)
This is the most important window. The fireside is the centrepiece of the evening, and the two readings (by my daughters) are the emotional anchors. Coverage must include:

My eldest daughter MCing — at the lectern, with the room visible behind her
My younger daughter at the lectern reading from the prologue — at least one frame where she is mid-reading and the audience is visibly attentive
The fireside conversation — multiple angles, ideally including: a wide of both speakers with the dhow on the table between them; close portraits of me mid-thought, mid-laugh, and mid-listen; close portraits of Chin-Ru hosting; and a frame that includes the audience leaning in
The Q&A — at least one wide of the room with a guest standing to ask a question
The signing queue — long line, books being signed, candid joy and connection
One clean signing portrait — me at the table, signing a book, audience visible behind

Iconic image
By the end of the night, I need one image that can serve as the permanent visual record of this launch. The strongest candidates are: me and Chin-Ru mid-fireside with the dhow in the foreground; my daughter at the lectern with the room in soft focus; or a wide of the packed Social Hall during the programme. The photographer is welcome to identify the iconic shot through their lens, but I need it to exist when the night ends.
Press-ready frames
At least 10 frames need to be press-ready by 8 am the morning after — wide-format, sharp, well-lit, suitable for newspaper picture desks. Captioned briefly. Delivered as a small selection alongside the main edited gallery (which can follow within a week).
Style and tone

Documentary, not staged. Posed group shots only when explicitly requested.
Warm, natural colour grading. Not overly stylised.
Available light where possible; flash used sparingly and never during the readings or fireside.
Quiet presence. The photographer should be largely invisible during the programme — no clicking shutters during the rendition, no movement during the fireside silences.

Numbers and delivery

Approximately 150–250 finished, edited frames for the main gallery
10–15 press-ready frames delivered by 8 am, 3 July
Full edited gallery delivered within 7 days of the event
Delivery via private gallery (Pic-Time, ShootProof, or similar), with download access for me and selective sharing rights
Full usage rights for me, including commercial use (book promotion, speaker reels, future editions, press, social, website, advertising). Photographer retains portfolio rights subject to my approval of which frames are used publicly.

Outline:

Draft Outline for Review
 
The goal of this video set is to create a polished, welcoming, and informative introduction to Incline for new hires. The videos should help people understand who Incline is, how the business works, what the culture feels like, and where to go for support as they get started.
 
The overall tone should feel like a company that is both high-performing and genuinely human.  Warm, local, and welcoming, while still clearly successful and growing quickly.  It should feel like “nice to meet you” from people who know exactly what they’re doing.  Professional, but not stiff.  Personable, but never performative.  There can be moments of lightness or personality, but nothing that feels forced or overly produced.  The goal is to create immediate trust and a sense of belonging, without losing clarity or credibility.  
 
Individual videos can be set in interview format if you’d like so that it breaks things up a bit.
 
1. CEO Welcome Video
Working title: Welcome to Incline
Suggested length: 3 - 5 minutes
Primary speaker: CEO
 
 
Purpose
This is the opening message for new hires. It should set the tone from the top and help people immediately understand that they are joining a company with a clear mission, strong standards, and a real sense of purpose.
 
 
Content outline: (Scripted/prompter used)
• Warm welcome to new hires
• Brief overview of Incline’s mission and what the company does
• Why the work matters
• What makes Incline distinctive in the market
• A few words about the kind of culture and mindset the company values
• What new hires can expect in their first few weeks
• Encouragement and excitement about their decision to join
 
 
 
Tone
• Direct and personable
• Confident but not stiff
• Aspirational
 
 
*Optional addition
At the end of the CEO video, include a short Executive Team Introduction montage rather than creating a separate standalone video.
 
 
 
 
1. Executive Team Introduction Montage
Working title: Meet the Executive Team
Suggested length: 2 - 4 minutes total
Primary speaker: Executive team members
Format: Short clips from each executive, likely 15–25 seconds each
 
 
Purpose
To make the leadership team feel visible, accessible, and human. This gives new hires quick context on who is who and what each leader owns.
 
 
Content outline
• Name
• Title
• Time at Incline
• What their team is responsible for
• Come to me or my team for… or You’ll work with us on…
 
 
 
Example format
“Hi, I’m [Name], [Title]. I’ve been with Incline for [X years]. My team focuses on [brief area]. You’ll likely interact with us when it comes to [X, Y, Z]. Welcome to Incline.”
 
 
Tone
• Clear and consistent
• Friendly and concise
• Professional but approachable
 
 
 
Notes
• Keep every clip formulaic for ease and consistency
• Use lower-third titles for name and role
• This works best as part of the CEO welcome rather than a separate long asset
 
 
 
 
 
1. Culture Video
Working title: The Incline Way
Suggested length: 3 - 4 minutes
Primary speaker: EVP HR
 
 
Purpose
To translate culture into something practical and believable. Not just values on a screen, but what people can actually expect from the workplace experience.
 
 
Content outline
• What Incline values in how people work together
• Expectations around communication, collaboration, accountability, and professionalism
• What support looks like at Incline
• How leaders and teams show up for one another
• What helps people succeed here
• What new hires should know about the employee experience
 
 
 
Tone
• Warm, grounded, and real
• Specific rather than vague
• Clear and relatable
 
 
 
Optional visual support
• B-roll of office and team interaction
• Light cutaways to moments of collaboration, meetings, or everyday work
• On-screen words only if they reinforce, not overwhelm
 
 
 
 
 
1. Business Model Overview
Working title: How Incline Works
Suggested length: 4 - 6 minutes
Primary speaker: Chief Risk Officer and Chief Legal Officer
Format: Tag-team conversation or lightly moderated interview
 
 
Purpose
To help new hires understand the business at a high level in plain English. This should answer the question: How does this company work, and how do the pieces fit together?
 
 
Content outline
• Simple overview of what Incline does
• How the business makes money or where value is created
• Key functions or moving parts within the organization
• Why risk and legal matter to the business model
• How different teams connect to one another
• What new hires should understand about decision-making, compliance, and risk awareness
 
 
 
Tone
• Clear and explanatory
• Conversational, not overly technical
• Confident and grounded
 
 
 
Suggested structure
• Intro: what the video will help new hires understand
• What Incline does in practical terms
• How the business is structured
• How risk and legal enable the business
• Why cross-functional understanding matters
• Closing advice for new hires
 
 
 
 
 
1. CFO Video
Working title: Every Role Drives the Business
Suggested length: 2 - 3 minutes
Primary speaker: CFO
 
 
Purpose
To help employees understand how their individual role connects to the overall health and success of the business.
 
 
Content outline
• How Incline makes money
• Every role contributes to business outcomes
• Operational excellence and thoughtful decision-making matter
• How strong performance supports long-term success
• The connection between day-to-day work and company performance
• Encouragement for employees to take ownership of their impact
 
 
 
Tone
• Clear and motivating
• Practical and grounded
• Focused on impact and ownership
 
 
 
 
 
1. Employee Welcome Video
Working title: Meet Incline
Suggested length: 4 - 6 minutes
Primary speaker: Incline employees
Format: 20–25 employees answering the same 5 questions
Style: Fast, upbeat, human, edited for energy and variety.  FUN.
 
 
Purpose
To showcase the people of Incline and give new hires an authentic sense of the team they are joining.
 
 
Content outline
1. What’s your name and role?
2. How long have you been at Incline?
3. What’s your favorite thing about working here?
4. What’s one piece of advice for a new hire?
5. What’s something that makes Incline unique?
 
 
 
Tone
• Energetic and authentic
• Welcoming and human
• Diverse in voice and perspective
 
 
 
Notes
• Keep answers short and punchy
• Include a mix of departments, tenure levels, and personalities
• Feature both newer hires and longer-tenured employees
 
 
 
Editing style
• Quick cuts
• Name and title lower thirds
• Light background music
• B-roll of people working, collaborating, and interacting
 
 
 
 
 
Recommended Final Video Set
 
1. Welcome to Incline, CEO
2. Meet the Executive Team, executive montage appended to CEO video
3. The Incline Way, CHRO
4. How Incline Works, Chief Risk Officer and Chief Legal Officer
5. Every Role Drives the Business, CFO
6. Meet Incline, employee spotlight montage
 
 
 
 
 
Production Notes
 
 
General approach
• Consistent visual style, framing, and lighting across all videos
• Clean, conversational delivery
• Branded lower thirds for names and titles
• Use of B-roll to add energy and context
 
 
 
Shoot day estimate
A single full day of filming might be feasible if all participants are scheduled efficiently and logistics are tightly coordinated. A second partial day may be required depending on availability, number of interviews, and desired amount of B-roll. 2 days recommended if also utilizing Production team for headshots. B-roll office stills.  
 
 
 
 
Voiceover and Narrative Support (Optional)
If we incorporate B-roll or need connective narration between segments, I am happy to provide voiceover support at no additional cost. I have a strong background in commercial voiceover and performance, which can help ensure consistency in tone, clarity, and delivery across the full video series.

Notes:
Photographer + Videographer Needed for Father-Son Retreat in the Colorado Mountains (June 24–27)

Looking for a skilled male photographer/videographer to document a father-son retreat in the mountains of Florissant, Colorado (about 90 minutes west of Colorado Springs).
Event: Ironwood — an immersive rite-of-passage retreat for fathers and their sons (ages 9–11)

Dates: Wednesday, June 24 (~4:00 PM start) through Saturday, June 27 (~1:00 PM end), 2026

Location: The Nature Place, Florissant, CO

Group Size: 12–15 father-son pairs (24–30 participants total)

What You'd Be Capturing:
This is not a standard corporate event or party. Ironwood is a deeply intentional experience designed around outdoor challenge, emotional connection, and transformation. The moments range from high-energy adventure to quiet, intimate ceremonies.

Here's what the retreat looks like:

Wednesday Evening: Arrival and welcome ceremony in a mountain lodge setting.

Thursday: Low ropes challenge course, orienteering/navigation exercises, identity-building conversations, and evening campfire circles.

Friday: The peak day — high ropes course (including a dramatic "Leap of Faith" element), this is the most cinematic day.

Saturday Morning: The emotional culmination — fathers read personal letters to their sons in a group ceremony, followed by a commissioning/closing circle.

Throughout the retreat, you'll also be capturing: mountain landscapes, candid father-son interactions, group meals, nature hikes, and the overall atmosphere of a Colorado mountain retreat.

What We Need:

Photography: High-quality edited photos of each father-son pair throughout the retreat — candid and documentary-style. These will be given to each family as a keepsake after the event.

Videography: Raw video footage capturing the full arc of the experience — from arrival to transformation. This footage will be used to produce a promotional video (editing may be handled separately, so raw footage delivery is perfectly acceptable). If you also offer editing and want to propose a highlight/recap video, we're open to that as well.

Drone/Aerial (optional): We have a DJI drone on-site that can be used to capture B-roll aerial footage of the mountain venue and outdoor activities. If you're comfortable flying it for some supplemental shots, great — but this is not a requirement.


Ideal Candidate:

Male (required — this is a men's retreat and we need you embedded naturally in the group)

Comfortable in rugged outdoor mountain settings for extended periods

Experience with documentary or storytelling-style event coverage (not just traditional event photography)

Able to capture emotionally sensitive moments with discretion and respect

Comfortable being on-site from Wednesday afternoon through Saturday midday (accommodations and meals provided on-site)

Based in or willing to travel to the Florissant/Colorado Springs/Denver area


What We Provide:
Private room with en-suite bathroom at the venue for the duration of the event

Notes:
Scene 1: The Village Morning 🌄
In a peaceful village, birds were chirping and people were starting their day.
An old but cheerful grandmother zoomed past on her noisy scooter.
“Vroooom!”
Everyone laughed and said,
“Look! Motor Dadi is here!”
Scene 2: Dadi the Hero 🛵
Motor Dadi wore big glasses and a bright shawl. She loved helping people.
She delivered vegetables, medicines, and sometimes even gave kids rides.
Children waved,
“Dadi! Fast ride!”
She laughed, “Hold tight!”
Scene 3: The Injured Pigeon 🕊️
One afternoon, while riding through the market, Dadi saw a small pigeon sitting quietly near the road.
It looked weak and couldn’t fly.
Dadi stopped her scooter immediately.
“Oh no, little one… you’re hurt.”
Scene 4: Rescue Time ❤️
Dadi gently picked up the pigeon and placed it in her basket.
“Don’t worry, I’m here,” she said softly.
She drove home carefully so the pigeon wouldn’t get scared.
Scene 5: Care and Love 🏡
At home, Dadi made a cozy bed for the pigeon using soft cloth.
She gave it grains and water.
Every day, she talked to it like a friend.
“Get well soon, my little guest,” she smiled.
Scene 6: Recovery 💪
Days passed. The pigeon slowly became stronger.
One morning, it flapped its wings…
Flap! Flap!
Dadi clapped happily,
“Good! You can fly again!”
Scene 7: Goodbye Moment 😢
Dadi opened the window.
“It’s time for you to go back to the sky,” she said gently.
The pigeon looked at her for a moment… then flew away.
Dadi felt a little lonely but smiled.
Scene 8: A Sweet Surprise 🌟
The next day, something amazing happened.
The pigeon came back!
It sat on Dadi’s scooter and made a soft sound,
“Coo… coo…”
Dadi laughed,
“Oh! You came back to me!”
Scene 9: Best Friends Forever 🤝
From that day on, the pigeon became Dadi’s travel partner.
Whenever Dadi rode her scooter, the pigeon sat in front like a tiny captain.
People in the village smiled,
“Look! Motor Dadi and her pigeon!”
Scene 10: Happy Ending 🌈
Now, Dadi was never alone.
She had a loyal little friend who always returned to her.
And the village learned something beautiful:
Kindness creates friendship that never flies away.

धुरंधर में सिर्फ एक सर था लेकिन यहां दो-दो मिलेंगे। विजय सेतुपति नाम तो सुना ही होगा। पूरे करियर में जितना सिनेमा सब का सब एक दूसरे से अलग। जो फिल्में यह करते हैं वो बाकी एक्टर्स करने का सोच तक नहीं खत्म कर सकते हो और बिना किसी टेंशन hotstar पर हिंदी डबिंग में इजीली देख सकते हो। इस बार खास चीज यह है कि शो की एंडिंग ओपन एंडिंग है। मतलब देखने वाला खुद इसका क्लाइमेक्स डिसाइड करेगा। लेकिन सब कुछ न्यूज़ आई है। यह पुलिस स्टेशन हमेशा के लिए बंद होने जा रहा है। और रीजन यह है कि गांव में कोई केस आता ही नहीं है। जहां क्राइम ही नहीं वहां पुलिस की जरूरत किसको है? और फिर बजती है फोन की घंटी। दूसरी तरफ से जो आवाज आती है, वह सुनकर इन तीनों लोगों के होश उड़ जाते हैं। आपके भी उड़ जाएंगे। उसी गांव के सुनसान खेत में एक बकरी घुमाने वाले लड़के को मिलता है एक इंसान का कटा हुआ सर और मरते वक्त यह आदमी अच्छे खासे तरीके से हंस रहा था। लेकिन उससे भी अजीब बात यह है वहां सिर्फ कटा हुआ सर मौजूद है। उसका बाकी शरीर एकदम गायब है। पूरे जंगल में उसकी बॉडी का कोई निशान खून तक नहीं है। और सबसे हैरान करने वाली बात यह सर अकेला नहीं है। इसके ठीक बगल में रखी है एक चिट्ठी और उसका आखिरी मैसेज साफ-साफ लिखा हुआ है। जो भी इस सर को दफनाएगा उसे पूरे ₹ लाख मिलेंगे और हेलो नो चीटिंग। मरता हुआ आदमी झूठ नहीं बोलता क्योंकि पैसे सुपर हीरो दिया था। मिलिन सोमन और विजय सेतुपति जिस वक्त सीरीज में यह दोनों आपस में जुड़ते हैं, शो का लेवल लाइट ह्यूमर ड्रामा से डार्क क्राइम थ्रिलर में चेंज हो जाता है। और बताने की जरूरत नहीं है जहां विजय सेतुपति हैं, वहां एक्टिंग की शिकायत नहीं हो सकती है। इतना रियल, इतना लोकल, इतना नेचुरल सेटअप है इस शो का जैसे केरला पहुंच गए हो। बस एक दिक्कत जो आपको महसूस होगी शो में बहुत सारे एक्स्ट्रा कैरेक्टर्स दिखाए हैं जिनसे जुड़ी अनवांटेड स्टोरी जो फालतू में छह एपिसोड की कहानी को 10 तक खींच ले जाती है और जितना सुनने में यह कटा हुआ सर का कांसेप्ट मिस्टीरियस लगता है उतना इसको यूज़ नहीं किया गया जिस वजह से यह सीरीज थोड़ा स्लो लग सकती है आपको पांच में से तीन स्टार्स मिलेंगे स्टोरी टेलिंग एक्टिंग और बहुत कम लेकिन शॉकिंग एक्शन के लिए नेगेटिव्स एक्स्ट्रा कैरेक्टर्स जिनकी जरूरत नहीं थी प्लस कछुए की स्पीड से फास्ट को दिखाना अच्छा टाइम पास फैमिली कंटेंट है कोई एडल्ट व्गर सीन नहीं है विजय सेतुप फैंस को शिकायत का मौका नहीं मिलेगा। टेक केयर। बाय-बाय।

A young boy named Chiku loved playing badminton and spent every day happily playing with his friends. His father was also a great badminton player, and every evening they used to play together, creating beautiful memories.
One day, Chiku’s badminton racket suddenly broke, and he became very sad. His father was no longer in this world, and the loss made him feel even more emotional.
Slowly, Chiku walked into his father’s room and saw his father’s old badminton racket hanging on the wall. With tears in his eyes, he took the racket and went outside to play again.
As he played, he felt as if his father was right there with him, guiding him in every shot.
With hope in his heart, Chiku made a promise to himself — one day, he would become a great badminton player just like his father. And from that day on, he practiced every single day with determination.

[h2]Company Overview[/h2]
[color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]RxFood is a clinically proven, AI-powered medical nutrition therapy platform developed by physicians and registered dietitians. The platform bridges the gap between clinical nutrition science and everyday eating — enabling clinicians to prescribe nutrition like a diagnostic test and empowering patients to track, understand, and improve their diet with ease.[/color]


[h2]Core Product[/h2]
[color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]The RxFood app allows users to log meals by taking photos. AI instantly identifies and analyses food items, generating detailed nutrition and diet quality reports tailored to specific health conditions (diabetes, cardiovascular disease, obesity, kidney disease, etc.). Clinicians receive rich, customisable reports on patient intake — completing a full dietary history up to 3x faster than traditional methods.[/color]


[h2]Key Proof Points[/h2]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]97% of users say RxFood is the easiest nutrition tracking platform they have used[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]94% of users say RxFood helped them make meaningful nutrition changes[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Clinically shown to lower A1c by 0.8% in children with Type 1 diabetes after 3 months[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Accuracy comparable to research-grade databases (USDA / ESHA)[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]PHIPA / HIPAA compliant — patient data is never sold or shared[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Supports medical nutrition therapy billing codes and remote patient monitoring codes[/color]


[h2]Business Model[/h2]
[color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]RxFood operates a B2B2C model. It sells to healthcare organisations (hospitals, family health teams, insurers, employee wellness programmes) who then deploy RxFood to their patients or members. The end user (patient/member) experiences the product directly through the mobile app.[/color]


[h2]Audiences[/h2]
[ml][ul][li indent=0 align=left][color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Clinicians: physicians, dietitians, nurses, health coaches and other allied health professionals[/color][/li][li indent=0 align=left][color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Healthcare Organisations (B2B clients): hospitals, family health teams, insurance companies, employee wellness programmes[/color][/li][li indent=0 align=left][color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]End Users / Patients: people living with chronic disease or anyone seeking evidence-based nutrition support[/color][/li][/ul][/ml]

[h1]Brand & Creative Direction[/h1]

[h2]Brand Voice[/h2]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Evidence-based and credible — never gimmicky[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Warm and human — this is healthcare, not a fitness fad app[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Simple and clear — complex science made accessible[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Empowering — patients take ownership; clinicians gain superpowers[/color]


[h2]Visual Direction[/h2]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Clean, modern aesthetic with a clinical-meets-consumer feel[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Primary palette: deep greens, white, and soft neutrals[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Avoid generic stock footage of salads or gym workouts[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Authentic-feeling lifestyle footage: real meals, real clinical settings[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]App UI screencasts should be polished, using real product screens[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Motion graphics for data / analytics moments — make numbers feel exciting[/color]


[h2]Music & Audio[/h2]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Hero video: uplifting, modern, builds energy — not generic corporate[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Clinical demos: calm, professional, understated[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Product overviews: warm and approachable, mid-tempo[/color]


[h2]On-Screen Text[/h2]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Clean sans-serif typography — brand-consistent[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Key statistics and proof points should animate on screen[/color]
•     [color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Avoid cluttering the frame — let visuals breathe[/color]




[h2]Project Overview[/h2]


[b][color=rgb(85, 85, 85)]Duration[/color][/b]
[color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]1–3 minutes (target: ~2 minutes)[/color]
[b][color=rgb(85, 85, 85)]Format[/color][/b]

[b][color=rgb(85, 85, 85)]Audience[/color][/b]

[color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]Friendly, encouraging, easy to follow — accessible to all health literacy levels[/color]

[h2]Objective[/h2]
[color=rgb(34, 34, 34)]This is the first touchpoint many end users will have with RxFood. It needs to answer: What is RxFood? Why should I use it? How do I get started? It should build excitement and remove any friction or anxiety around trying a new health app.[/color]


[h2]Key Messages[/h2]
[ml][ul][li indent=0 align=left][b]Eating well just got easier.[/b] Snap a photo of your meal and RxFood does the rest — instant, accurate nutrition tracking in seconds.[/li][li indent=0 align=left][b]Understand your food, understand yourself.[/b] Get personalised nutrition reports built around your goals — whether you're managing a chronic condition, navigating hormonal changes, or simply wanting more energy and confidence in what you eat.[/li][li indent=0 align=left][b]Real guidance, not generic advice.[/b] Your AI assistant, MyFoods feature, and personalised insights help you make smarter choices every day — from grocery shopping to eating out.[/li][li indent=0 align=left][b]Want expert support?[/b] Book an RxFood dietitian and get the best of both worlds — cutting-edge technology plus a real human who knows your data, your goals, and your life.[/li][li indent=0 align=left][b]Science-backed. Clinically proven. Built for real life.[/b] RxFood is trusted by healthcare providers to help people like you make meaningful, lasting change.[/li][/ul][/ml]

ki kisi ko bina paaye bhi…

Corporate Filming Brief (APLGO, USA group of 250-300 people)

I’ll outline what we expect as the final result. We don’t just need general footage, we need to cover several specific deliverables. The main all day event is on April 18 from 8:30am-6pm. Then a recognition ceremony at 8pm-10:30pm. on the 19th we're having a group of about 50 go to SeaWorld from 8:30am-3pm and then in the evening 6pm-8pm we have a VIP dinner of about 30 people.

1. One-minute teaser (urgent)

Goal: a dynamic highlight reel of the entire day including training, emotions, recognition and energy.

Keep natural audio from the camera and also add music. The editing should feel fast, lively and engaging.

Deadline: the final video must be delivered the next day after filming.

Important for the videographer: film throughout the entire day, but always keep in mind that we need strong 5–10 second “hero moments” that can be quickly edited into a teaser.

1. Final event recap (up to 5 minutes)

This is the main video showing how the Fiesta went.

Length: up to 5 minutes.

Format, two options.

Option A (preferred): classic recap with voice-over narration. We align with you on the script and structure. You write narration based on the footage and edit accordingly.

Option B: build the video around interviews.

Record short interviews with 10–15 guests and associates. Ask them why they are here, why they are with the company, what makes it unique, what the atmosphere is like and how their business or life will change after this event.

These answers will form the storyline.

Deadline: within one week after the event.

1. Raw footage (archive materials)

It is very important for us to keep everything.

We need all speaker presentations, the president’s appearance, the full recognition ceremony, the venue atmosphere and decor, and all additional footage captured. Everything.

Delivery: upload everything to cloud storage such as Google Drive or Dropbox and share the link. This will be part of the company archive, so the footage must be preserved.

1. Social media content (vertical and reels)

We need real-time content during the event.

Vertical footage: please film additional content on an iPhone or in a format suitable for vertical cropping. Focus on details, speakers, the audience and emotions.

Important: send vertical clips to our chat in real time as files. Do not wait until the end of the day.

Daily reels: at the end of each filming day we need a ready-to-post reel with the best moments of that day.

Filming at SeaWorld

Here we need three types of content.

One-minute teaser (emotions)

A very dynamic edit with fast cuts including rides, faces, laughter, and food. This should capture pure energy and impressions of our associates. Music-driven with minimal talking.

Two to three minute story video

Focus on meaning and storytelling.

Film associates near the castle, rides and roller coasters. Capture them sharing how their life changed after joining the company, how they now live a more exciting and joyful life and the value of being surrounded by like-minded people.

This video should combine dynamic Disneyworld visuals with authentic emotional interview moments.

Vertical content for social media

Short engaging vertical clips focused on energy, emotions and atmosphere.

Notes:
I came across your company because we at Knorr-Bremse Rail Systems Denmark are currently looking for a videographer on short notice for our workshop in Aarhus.

Knorr-Bremse Rail Systems Denmark is part of the Knorr-Bremse Group, a global leader in braking systems and rail vehicle technologies. In Denmark, we focus on maintaining, repairing and upgrading rail components such as wheelsets, bogies and braking systems. Currently, we’re planning a so called ground test on a bogie. During this test, sensors are mounted on the wheelset bearings to assess their condition and detect potential defects. The setup is quite dynamic, as the wheels rotate to simulate a moving bogie. We’d like to capture this process in a short 2 - 4 minute video that we can later use for marketing purposes. I
 
For the video, we would like to take the viewer on a short journey – from the mechanical component to the digital insights. Ideally, the storyline would include:
•	a damaged or worn bearing as a starting point
•	the installation of the bearing onto the axle (if realistic within the timing – we are currently checking internally)
•	how our technology monitors the bearing condition
•	the data and graphs appearing on the screen
•	a transition showing how traditional mechanical work connects to digital diagnostics

To achieve this, we are looking for someone who not only brings the full filming equipment but also has a good eye for technical setups and can guide us a bit regarding what works visually and what resonates well with customers. Ideally, someone with experience capturing industrial or technical processes who can help us make the video both accurate and engaging.

We therefore need someone who can film on April 14 and 15 (approximately 4 hours each day; exact times to be confirmed) and afterwards also handle the editing of the final video.
If the timeframe works for you and you’re interested, we’d appreciate receiving a non binding quote.

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out at any time. Looking forward to hearing from you!

[h2]OFFICIAL TRAILER SCRIPT[/h2]
[h3][i]My Life from Fenway to Phoenix[/i][/h3]
[b]Length:[/b] ~90 seconds

[b]BLACK SCREEN.[/b]
Silence.
Then — the faint sound of a baseball crowd.
[b]NARRATION (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“Before the war… before the wounds… I thought loyalty was simple.”[/quote][b]CUT TO:[/b]
Grainy archival footage of [b]Fenway Park[/b], late afternoon sun. Fans rising from wooden seats. A crack of the bat.
[b]NARRATION (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“You showed up. You stayed. You didn’t quit.”[/quote][b]CUT TO:[/b]
Black-and-white photos: a boy, a neighborhood, a family dinner table.
[b]MUSIC:[/b] Soft, piano-driven. Reflective.

[b]SMASH CUT TO SILENCE.[/b]
A transport plane door closing.
[b]NARRATION (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“Nobody tells you that the things that shape you early… can carry you into places you never planned to go.”[/quote][b]CUT TO:[/b]
Jungle foliage. Boots hitting mud. Helicopter blades overhead — heard, not seen.
Quick, restrained flashes:
[ml][ul][li indent=0 align=left]A young Marine’s face (shadowed)[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Hands tightening on a rifle[/li][li indent=0 align=left]Rain on a helmet[/li][/ul][/ml][b]TEXT ON SCREEN:[/b]
 [i]A Vietnam Marine Corps Veteran[/i]
[b]NARRATION (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“Vietnam didn’t make me brave.[/quote][quote] It taught me how fragile everything really is.”[/quote][b]CUT TO BLACK.[/b]
A heartbeat.

[b]CUT TO:[/b]
A hospital wristband. A Purple Heart citation (no lingering).
[b]NARRATION (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“I came home alive.[/quote][quote] That was supposed to be the happy ending.”[/quote][b]CUT TO:[/b]
1970s street footage. A divided America. Headlines. Protest signs passing by a car window.
[b]NARRATION (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“But coming home was harder than leaving.”[/quote][b]MUSIC BUILDS SLIGHTLY.[/b]
[b]CUT TO:[/b]
Fast but controlled montage:
[ml][ul][li indent=0 align=left]Newspaper presses running (Chicago Tribune era)[/li][li indent=0 align=left]An airplane cabin / SkyMall catalog[/li][li indent=0 align=left]A patent drawing[/li][li indent=0 align=left]A man writing alone at a desk[/li][/ul][/ml][b]NARRATION (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“So I built a life.[/quote][quote] Quietly.[/quote][quote] Like a lot of us did.”[/quote][b]CUT TO:[/b]
Wide desert shot at sunrise — [b]Phoenix[/b].
The same man, older now, sitting still.
[b]NARRATION (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“This isn’t a story about war.”[/quote]Beat.
[quote]“It’s a story about what stays with you… long after the noise fades.”[/quote][b]TITLE CARD:[/b]
 [b]MY LIFE FROM FENWAY TO PHOENIX[/b]
[b]TEXT ON SCREEN:[/b]
 [i]A Limited Episodic Documentary Series[/i]
[b]FINAL LINE (V.O.):[/b]
[quote]“I didn’t write this to explain myself.[/quote][quote]I wrote it so someone else wouldn’t feel alone.”[/quote][b]FADE OUT.[/b]

Sam
